from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Vectors live on a Cartesian grid.", "Arrows start at the origin point.", "Coordinates [x, y] define the endpoint."]
        self.setup_layout("Coordinate Representation (The Grid System)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Grid setup
        cartesian_grid = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=3.2,
            y_length=3.2,
            axis_config={"color": "#D3D3D3"}
        )
        # Fix 38: Place grid in area
        self.place_in_area(cartesian_grid, 'B3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg
        # Note: The storyboard says to place a vector 'v' from origin to (2,3) in green (#00FF00)
        # Using SVGMobject for the referenced asset.
        asset_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(asset_icon, 'A1', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(cartesian_grid), FadeIn(asset_icon))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#D3D3D3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        origin = cartesian_grid.c2p(0, 0)
        vec_end = cartesian_grid.c2p(2, 3)
        vector_arrow = Arrow(start=origin, end=vec_end, color="#00FF00", buff=0)
        # Fix 40: Scale/place arrow
        self.place_in_area(vector_arrow, 'C3', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(vector_arrow))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        dashed_x = DashedLine(cartesian_grid.c2p(2, 3), cartesian_grid.c2p(2, 0), color="#FFA500")
        dashed_y = DashedLine(cartesian_grid.c2p(2, 3), cartesian_grid.c2p(0, 3), color="#FFA500")
        
        coordinate_label = Text("[2, 3]", font_size=20, color="#FFA500")
        # Fix 39: Place coordinate label
        self.place_at_grid(coordinate_label, 'C4', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(dashed_x), Create(dashed_y), Write(coordinate_label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFA500")

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Vector Addition (The Tip-to-Tail Rule)", [
            "Adding vectors follows simple rules.",
            "Connect the tail to the tip.",
            "The result is the final path."
        ])
        
        # Define vectors
        v = Vector(RIGHT*1.5 + UP*0.5, color=WHITE)
        w = Vector(RIGHT*0.5 + UP*1.5, color=WHITE)
        
        v_label = MathTex(r"\\vec{v}", color=WHITE).next_to(v.get_center(), UP)
        w_label = MathTex(r"\\vec{w}", color=WHITE).next_to(w.get_center(), RIGHT)

        # Assets
        ruler = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg")
        pencil = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pencil.svg")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(ruler, 'B6', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(v, 'C3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(w, 'D4', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(ruler), Create(v), Write(v_label), Create(w), Write(w_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # Move w so its tail meets the tip of v
        new_w_start = v.get_end()
        w_vec = w.get_end() - w.get_start()
        w_new_pos = new_w_start + w_vec / 2
        
        self.play(
            w.animate.move_to(w_new_pos),
            w_label.animate.move_to(w_new_pos + RIGHT*0.5 + UP*0.5)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        
        resultant = Vector(v.get_vector() + w.get_vector(), color=RED)
        resultant.move_to(v.get_start() + resultant.get_vector()/2)
        res_label = MathTex(r"\\vec{v}+\\vec{w}", color=RED)
        self.place_in_area(res_label, 'E2', 'F4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(pencil, 'F5', scale_factor=0.3)
        
        self.play(Create(resultant), Write(res_label), FadeIn(pencil))
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Scaling Vectors (Multiplication)", [
            "Scaling stretches or shrinks vectors.",
            "Multiplying changes the arrow length.",
            "Negatives reverse the vector direction."
        ])
        
        # Define base vector
        v = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 2, color=WHITE, buff=0)
        self.place_at_grid(v, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\\vec{v}", color=WHITE).next_to(v.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Assets
        compass = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg")
        spring = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/spring.svg")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(compass, 'C4', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(v), Write(v_label), FadeIn(compass))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(TEAL))
        v2 = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 4, color=TEAL, buff=0)
        self.place_at_grid(v2, 'D2', scale_factor=0.8)
        v2_label = MathTex(r"2\\vec{v}", color=TEAL).next_to(v2.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis & Summary", ["Vectors model movement in physics.", "They are instructions for space.", "We use them everywhere today."])
        
        # Elements for the summary visualization
        arrow1 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=BLUE)
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color=GREEN)
        resultant = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=(RIGHT+UP)*1.5, color=GOLD)
        
        # Group them
        summary_group = VGroup(arrow1, arrow2, resultant)
        self.place_in_area(summary_group, 'C3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(arrow1), FadeIn(arrow2), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(resultant), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(summary_group.animate.set_color(GOLD), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GOLD))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(summary_group), FadeOut(self.title))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Vectors: The Language of Space
outline.target_audience: High school students or introductory undergraduate students

sections.title: What is a Vector? (The Arrow Analogy)
sections.content: Introduce vectors as directed line segments representing both magnitude (length) and direction. Contrast them with scalars (simple numbers).
sections.example: A hiker moving 5km North: '5km' is the scalar magnitude, 'North' is the direction, and the arrow shows the displacement.

sections.title: Coordinate Representation (The Grid System)
sections.content: Explain how vectors are positioned on a Cartesian plane using [x, y] coordinates. Visualizing the vector as an arrow starting at the origin (0,0) and ending at point (x, y).
sections.example: A video game character jumping: The vector [3, 4] means moving 3 units right and 4 units up on the game screen.

sections.title: Vector Addition (The Tip-to-Tail Rule)
sections.content: Explain adding vectors visually. Place the 'tail' of the second vector at the 'tip' of the first. The resulting vector connects the starting point to the final destination.
sections.example: A boat crossing a river: One vector is the boat's speed, the other is the river's current. Combining them shows the boat's actual diagonal path.

sections.title: Scaling Vectors (Multiplication)
sections.content: Define scalar multiplication. Multiplying a vector by a number stretches or shrinks it. If the scalar is negative, the vector points in the opposite direction.
sections.example: A superhero 'Flash' running: If his speed vector is [2, 0], multiplying by 3 results in [6, 0]—a longer arrow representing higher speed.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
sections.content: Briefly recap how vectors form the backbone of graphics, physics, and AI. Emphasize that vectors are just 'instructions for movement' in a space.
sections.example: Connecting the concepts: Imagine a drone delivery path as a series of added vectors, mapped on a grid, scaled by wind speed, landing precisely at the target.
